title: Eviction Balance Controller and Sampled Utilization Inspector for Dedicated Fleets
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Introduce Eviction Balance Controller to reduce unnecessary tenant evictions by smoothing decommits across a soft window. Add Sampled Utilization Inspector: low-overhead agent-side sampling that improves fleet utilization signals and reduces noisy eviction triggers. Metrics: dedicated/eviction_rate_smoothed, dedicated/sample_util_p50/p90, dedicated/eviction_penalty_curve. Rollout: staged canary across 3 fleets, opt-in flag for legacy allocator.
description: Context: In several recent incidents we observed oscillatory tenant evictions driven by noisy instantaneous utilization samples from the admission controller. Motivation: reduce user-facing throttles and preserve committed throughput while still reclaiming capacity when needed. This PR introduces two coordinated components: 1) Eviction Balance Controller (EBC) that applies a soft-decommit window with a configurable penalty curve and fairness drift limiter to spread eviction decisions across time and tenants, and 2) Sampled Utilization Inspector (SUI), a low-overhead agent-side sampler that feeds percentile-based utilization signals to the autoscaler instead of relying on single-sample probes. Key design points: EBC computes an eviction_score = (util_delta * penalty_multiplier(time_since_last_eviction) + backlog_factor) with a tunable sigmoid penalty curve to avoid immediate repeated evictions; it emits an intended_decommit set which the allocator reconciler gates through proportional backfill heuristics. SUI samples targets at 50ms intervals for a rolling 1m window and reports p50/p90/p99 to the headroom controller; sampling is probabilistic (per-core token bucket) to bound CPU and bandwidth. Compatibility: the controller implements an opt-in feature flag dedicated.eviction_balance_v2; when disabled the system falls back to legacy immediate-evict path. Observability: new metrics (dedicated/eviction_rate_smoothed, dedicated/eviction_intent_queue, dedicated/sample_util_p50/p90/p99, dedicated/eviction_penalty_curve) and traces for decision provenance. Testing: unit tests for penalty curve mapping and invariants, integration tests simulating churn and degraded headroom, load tests running on perf-lab with synthetic bursts showing a 37% reduction in user-visible throttles and 12% less tail-latency for reserved tenants. Rollout plan: 1) internal canary on perf-lab cluster, 2) staged rollout to two non-critical customer fleets with A/B routing for 48h, 3) gradual global roll to Dedicated fleets with 1% increments and automatic rollback on SLO regression. Risks and mitigations: mis-calibrated penalty curve could delay required evictions; mitigation includes safe-fail override that enforces hard-evict when headroom drops below absolute_threshold. Backwards compatibility: SUI falls back to legacy metrics on older agents.

notes_for_ops: Default penalty_curve is conservative: scale on a per-fleet basis using dedicated.eviction_penalty.sigmoid.k and .midpoint
To force legacy behavior set dedicated.eviction_balance_v2=false in fleet config
If observing delayed reclamation set absolute_threshold in allocator to 3% to trigger hard-evict override
Dashboard: ops can monitor dedicated/eviction_rate_smoothed and dedicated/sample_util_p90 to detect under-collection
